title: #16 D-099: `actl dag after gA --add|--drop gB` puts a group after another, also when its tickets are merged
objective: The main session can put group A after group B, or drop such an edge, with `actl dag after gA --add|--drop gB --reason R`, in one checked pool write that records the change on both groups, documented next to `actl dag dep/move`.
outline: devloop/core/dagedit.py: a check and an apply for the group edge, beside check()/apply() (suggested after_check(data, a, b, why, add) -> refusal line or None, and after_apply(tx, a, by, why, add=None, drop=None) -> refusal line or None), in item 6's order; the cycle check runs chain.cycle on Snapshot(copy.deepcopy(data.raw)) with the edge added (as check() does for dep/move), so a refusal writes nothing. The write: dag = tx.data.raw['dag']; edges = dag.setdefault('group_after', {}); change the list; tx.put_dag(dag); event(gA, ...) and event(gB, ...) from core.pool with by/why; tx.put_group for both. Reuse the edge reader of the chain ticket this depends on (e.g. chain.after_edges) when it has one. A group's job is the group record's 'job' field: None or a dict whose 'kind' is 'regression', 'fixer', ... devloop/dag_edit.py: a third subparser 'after' (positional A; --add/--drop mutually exclusive and required; --reason; --by default 'main-session'); the output lines of item 1 (no '#' before group ids); pool commit message e.g. 'dag: g1 after g3 (main-session)'; the module docstring gets the two usage lines. bin/actl: the TABLE line 'dag dep|move …' becomes 'dag dep|move|after …'. Docs per item 8 (README row and the 'Only the main session changes the DAG by hand' paragraph; CLAUDE.md one line after the `actl dag move` line). Do not touch docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/VISION.md (hard_block paths). Do not name anything `group_order` (test_chain.DagOrderUnits.test_no_code_sorts_groups_by_the_digits_of_the_id scans every devloop line for it).
test_plan: Verifier: cases for acceptance 4, 5 (pr with a merged member; fixing with a fixer job; stuck), 6 (one case per sentence a-f, plus the accepted drop of an edge to a landed B with its event on B), 7 (i) and (ii), 8 and 9, in a new class T<this ticket's id>Acceptance(LoopCase) in tests_devloop/test_dag_edit.py between class T125Acceptance and the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block (no other open ticket edits this file). Copy T125Acceptance's helpers into the class (fixture, dag, head, writes, clean, ok, refused, last_line, events, by_why); do not subclass T125Acceptance (its cases would run twice). Group records: tx.put_group({'id', 'branch': 'int/'+gid, 'state', 'members', 'fix_round': 0, 'job': None or {'kind': 'regression'|'fixer', 'stamp': 'x'}, 'created': STAMP}); tickets through self.add(N, state=..., group=gid, target='int/'+gid, deps=[...]). Any group_after a case needs before the command runs (item 6e already-set, 6f with a landed B) is written with self.pool.update(lambda tx: tx.put_dag(dict(tx.data.raw['dag'], group_after={...})), ...) AFTER every self.add() (the harness's add rewrites dag.json with only 'tickets' until the sibling ticket lands). No controller runs in these cases, so a fixture job is never reaped. Read dag.json from self.snap().raw['dag']. Item 8 reads bin/actl --help (as T125's test_actl_dag_runs_the_script_and_help_lists_it), devloop/README.md split on '\n\n' and on lines, and CLAUDE.md lines (HOME from loop_harness). Item 9 runs os.path.join(HOME, 'bin', 'actl') with cwd=self.proj and env=self.env. Every case is red before the change: dag_edit.py has no 'after' subcommand today (argparse exits 2 with two stderr lines) and the docs lack the texts. Expected values come from this ticket. Each dag_edit run takes well under a second; the class runs in seconds. Implementer: items 1-3 are covered by the verifier's walk; unit tests only for helpers it adds.
notes: Depends on new-1: the cycle refusal through edges (item 7) and the 'chain:' line (items 4, 5, 9) need the chain to count group_after. Group g11 with its siblings (issue #16 follow-ups); its files (dag_edit.py, core/dagedit.py, bin/actl, test_dag_edit.py, CLAUDE.md, README row 46 and the 'Only the main session' paragraph) are not edited by #134-#138. Design decisions: (1) adding an edge that is already set is refused, like `dep --add` of a dependency N already has; (2) a group in pr, fixing (even with a fixer job) or stuck may be reordered, because D-099's own list of what refuses is 'a regression running, verified, landed, cancelled'; after a fixer round the group returns to pr and its next regression starts only through advance_groups, the only caller of start_regression, which checks chain.waits_for; (3) the cycle refusal checks the whole changed copy, like dagedit.check for dep/move; --drop never checks for a cycle (removing an edge cannot make one); (4) events go on both groups even when B is landed, as the request asks. Out of scope: the board offering this action (D-096), reordering a group whose regression has started.
acceptance: 1 (CLI): `python3 devloop/dag_edit.py after A --add B --reason R [--by NAME]` and `... after A --drop B --reason R [--by NAME]` (--add and --drop mutually exclusive, one required; --by defaults to 'main-session'); `actl dag after ...` runs it (bin/actl already passes every argument to dag_edit.py). On success: exit 0, exactly one new pool commit, pool working copy clean; the first stdout line is 'A after B' (add) or 'A no longer after B' (drop); the last stdout line is 'chain: ' followed by core.chain.order of the pool after the change joined with ', '.

2 (storage): --add appends B to dag.json's group_after[A] (creating `group_after` and the list when missing); --drop removes B from that list and removes the key A when the list becomes empty. dag.json's `tickets` and every other top-level key stay as they were; no ticket file changes.

3 (events): every success appends one history row to group A and one to group B with event 'dag: A after B' (add) or 'dag: A no longer after B' (drop), 'by' = the --by value and 'why' = the --reason text; B gets its row also when B is landed or cancelled (drop of an edge to it).

4 (fixture walk): groups g1, g2, g3 open with the same created stamp (so natural id order), tickets #1, #2, #3 ready in them, no dependencies. `after g1 --add g3 --reason r` -> exit 0, first line 'g1 after g3', last line 'chain: g3, g1, g2', dag.json group_after == {'g1': ['g3']}, g1 and g3 each have exactly one 'dag: g1 after g3' event with by 'main-session' and why 'r', g2 has none. Then `after g1 --drop g3 --reason r2 --by alice` -> exit 0, first line 'g1 no longer after g3', last line 'chain: g1, g2, g3', 'g1' not in dag.json's group_after, g1 and g3 each have exactly one 'dag: g1 no longer after g3' event with by 'alice' and why 'r2'.

5 (groups whose tickets are merged can be reordered - the point of D-099): with g2 and g3 as in item 4 and g1 in state pr with #1 merged (target 'int/g1'), `after g1 --add g3 --reason r` exits 0 with last line 'chain: g3, g1, g2'; the same holds for g1 in state fixing with job {'kind': 'fixer', 'stamp': 'x'} and for g1 in state stuck. Only a job whose kind is 'regression' refuses (item 6d).

6 (refusals): exit 2, exactly one stderr line 'dag: <sentence>', pool HEAD unchanged and working copy clean; checked in this order: (a) --reason missing or blank: '--reason is required and must not be blank'; (b) A is not a group: 'group <A> does not exist', else B is not a group: 'group <B> does not exist'; (c) A == B: '<A> cannot be after itself'; (d) for --add and --drop: A's job has kind 'regression': 'group <A> has a regression running: its order no longer changes', else A's state is verified, landed or cancelled: 'group <A> is <state>: its order no longer changes'; (e) --add only: B already in group_after[A]: '<A> is already set after <B>', else B's state is landed or cancelled: 'group <B> is <state>: <A> cannot wait for it', else core.chain.cycle of an in-memory copy with the edge added is not None: 'the group order would be a cycle: ' + ' -> '.join(that cycle); (f) --drop only: B not in group_after[A]: '<A> is not set after <B>'. Dropping an existing edge to a landed or cancelled B is accepted (exit 0, item 3).

7 (cycles): (i) through a ticket dependency: groups g1 {#1}, g2 {#2}, g3 {#3 with depends_on ['1']} open, same created stamp: `after g1 --add g3 --reason r` is refused with 'the group order would be a cycle: g1 -> g3 -> g1'; (ii) through another edge: on groups as in item 4, `after g3 --add g1 --reason r` succeeds, then `after g1 --add g3 --reason r` is refused with 'the group order would be a cycle: g1 -> g3 -> g1'.

8 (docs): `bin/actl --help` has a line starting '  dag dep|move|after' (the TABLE line for dag_edit.py, its description now also naming groups); in devloop/README.md the table row that starts with '| `actl dag dep N --add M` / `--drop M` / `actl dag move N --to gK|new`' keeps that start, stays one row (no new row: test_groups.DagEditUnits.test_item8_docs checks the rows around it) and also contains '`actl dag after gA --add gB`'; the paragraph that starts with 'Only the main session changes the DAG by hand' contains 'actl dag after' and 'D-099' (with what it refuses; no new paragraph between 'Groups form one chain' and it); in CLAUDE.md the line right after the line containing '`actl dag move N --to gK|new --reason "…"`' contains '把整組排到另一組後面是 `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "…"`(票已合入的組也可以)' (written as '  把整組排到另一組後面是 `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "…"`(票已合入的組也可以)。', two-space indent, same bullet).
9 (actl): `bin/actl dag after g1 --add g3 --reason r` run in the test project exits 0 and its last stdout line is 'chain: g3, g1, g2' (fixture of item 4).

vision: 目的與成功指標: 每張票需要我介入幾次 and 等我處理的事積了多少 (down): in T (2026-11-24) the owner's order for g63, g70, g78 could not be set at all; now one command per group, without an opener run (about 1-3 US dollars each, D-096, inferred) and without cancelling and reopening merged groups.

request:
# `actl dag` can change the order of groups (docs/DECISIONS.md D-099; follow-up of GitHub issue #16)

The user's ruling (2026-11-24, verbatim in D-099): 「Ok Dag 也要允許群組順序改動」. Read D-096, D-098 and D-099 first, and the `actl dag` code from #125 (devloop/dag_edit.py, devloop/core/dagedit.py) and #122 (devloop/core/chain.py). Tests go in tests_devloop/test_dag_edit.py and tests_devloop/test_chain.py using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

Why: in T (2026-11-24) groups g63, g70 and g78 had all their tickets merged into their int branches, so `actl dag dep` and `actl dag move` refused them (frozen, D-089), and the main session could not put them after the group of #320 as the owner wanted. The chain order comes only from ticket dependencies and creation order, so there was no way to say "this group after that one".

Wanted:
1. A group-order edge kept in dag.json (a new field, e.g. `group_after: {"g63": ["g88"]}`), written only through the pool's validated write. core/chain.py builds the group graph from ticket dependencies plus these edges; the chain is a topological order of that graph with today's tie-break (created, then id).
2. `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "..."` puts group A after group B; `actl dag after gA --drop gB --reason "..."` removes an edge added this way (ticket dependencies are not touched). `--by` as the other `actl dag` commands (default main-session). The last stdout line is the chain after the change, like the other dag commands.
3. Refused with one line, nothing written: A or B does not exist; A == B; A has started or finished its regression (a regression job running, or state verified, landed or cancelled); B is landed or cancelled (adding is pointless; dropping an existing edge to a landed B is allowed); the edge makes a cycle with the ticket dependencies or other edges; `--drop` of an edge that is not there. A group whose tickets are merged (state pr, or open with merged members) can be reordered: that is the point.
4. Each change writes an event on both groups (who, why). When a group is moved behind another, nothing else changes now: when the earlier group lands, follow_main brings main into the later group's branch as today, and its regression runs after that (D-098).
5. Edges to a group that lands or is cancelled stay in dag.json as history but no longer constrain the order. Pool validation refuses a dag.json whose group edges make a cycle.
6. The board's DAG view and the idle/chain pages show the order as computed (no board action to change it, D-096). Document `actl dag after` in devloop/README.md next to `actl dag dep/move`, and add one line to CLAUDE.md 「怎麼做事」 after the `actl dag move` line: 「把整組排到另一組後面是 `actl dag after gA --add gB --reason "…"`(票已合入的組也可以)」.
- removes: the main session's inability to set the order of groups whose tickets are merged.
- Out of scope: the board offering this action; reordering a group that has started its regression.
